course_name_original: Urbanismo e Instalaciones en la Planta Industrial
course_name_en: Urban Planning and Facilities in Industrial Plants
prerequisites: Review and clear concepts of Physics, particularly Mechanics and Strength of Materials.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Communicate their conclusions and the underlying knowledge and reasons to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Acquire learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of urban planning and infrastructure.
Project, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
Direct, plan and supervise multidisciplinary teams.
Conduct research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Perform strategic planning and apply it to constructive and production, quality and environmental management systems.
Technically and economically manage industrial projects, facilities or plants.
Be able to exercise functions of general management, technical management and R+D+i project management in industrial plants.
Know, understand and apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Engineer.
Design, build and operate industrial plants.
Know construction, building, facilities, infrastructure and urban planning in the field of industrial engineering.

Project and design electrical and fluid installations, lighting, air conditioning and ventilation, energy saving and efficiency, acoustics, communications, home automation and smart buildings and security installations.

syllabus_topics: Environmental impact and sustainability in the industrial plant.

assessment_methods.method: Final exam on all topics covered
Evaluation of work developed in classroom practices
Evaluation of work developed in laboratory practices

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each of the evaluation parts. Non-face-to-face students will take a global questionnaire (20%), a final exam (60%), and a practical exam for practical class work (20%).
